Split from integrated App Live run 29704213912, which combines the exact heads of #16646, #16648, and #16649.

## Exact reproduction

The real packaged Electrobun build completes. `electrobun-packaged-regressions.e2e.spec.ts` then times out in `seedReturningInstallState()` because the full-shell route correctly has a foreground view scope and the test harness uses raw reserved `localStorage` writes:

```text
Last renderer result: {"ok":false,"error":"View \"chat\" denied storage: raw localStorage removeItem on reserved shell key \"elizaos:first-run:force-fresh\" — views use the surface storage facade (scope.storage); shell code uses shellLocalStorage"}

```

First failing site: `packages/app/test/electrobun-packaged/electrobun-packaged-regressions.e2e.spec.ts:917`; the following `eliza:*`/`elizaos:*` setItem calls are the same boundary violation.

The other launcher smoke failure in this run is downstream bridge starvation while the regression worker holds the main-window eval path.

## Acceptance

- Give the packaged harness a narrowly test-only privileged shell-storage seed path, or drive the equivalent real UI behavior.
- Do not weaken `surface-realm-broker`, expose a general privileged capability to views, add guard exclusions, or revert full-shell route coverage.
- Re-run packaged App Live with #16646/#16648/#16649 exact heads and show launcher routes, first-run/pairing, and notification observation together.

The independent exact-head packaged proofs for #16646 and #16649 already pass; this is cross-suite harness interference revealed only by the integrated run.

topIssues.title: bug(ui/chat): isolate parallel conversation turns and recover reload during send
topIssues.author: 0xSolace
topIssues.body:
## Summary

Live staging real-browser QA found two authoritative chat-integrity failures:

1. Two conversations used in parallel are not state-isolated. A queued/in-flight turn is correctly pinned to its target conversation for transport, but optimistic/streaming UI mutations still write through the single active `conversationMessages` state and can project a reply into the transcript selected later.
2. Reloading while a send is pending can leave the composer in a sending/stop state for more than 120 seconds instead of recovering from server truth within a bounded interval.

## Root cause / scope

`useChatSend` pins `conversationId` at enqueue (#10753), but `runQueuedChatSend` paints optimistic rows and stream/failure/terminal updates through unscoped `setConversationMessages`. Conversation identity is checked only around some history reloads. Navigation or a second conversation can therefore receive UI mutations owned by the first turn.

The reload path has no durable pending-turn recovery contract. A navigation reload tears down the client request, while the server turn may continue; the new page must start with an unlocked composer and reconcile the selected conversation rather than inheriting or recreating an unbounded pending state.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Parallel sends/navigation never project conversation A's optimistic row, tokens, terminal state, or reload into conversation B.
- [ ] A reload during a pending send restores an operable composer and preserves or settles the user turn from server truth within a bounded interval.
- [ ] Deterministic hook/component tests pin both races.
- [ ] Real Chromium staging evidence covers two parallel conversations and reload-during-send.
- [ ] No auth, API-key validation, pinned pre-stream HTTP 402 billing, or SSE-auth ordering changes.
- [ ] No warm-send median regression.

## Coordination

#16629 owns cold scope hydration only. This issue intentionally avoids its auth/shared-runtime files and any send prewarm changes.

topIssues.title: P0: terminally closed PGlite stays false-green and never auto-recovers
topIssues.author: 0xSolace
topIssues.body:
## Incident

On staging after fleet image recreation, a dedicated agent's process and HTTP health endpoint remained green for nearly two hours while its local PGlite adapter was terminally closed.

Authoritative runtime errors repeated continuously:

- `PGlite is closed`
- `Database is shutting down - operation rejected`
- SQL retries exhausted after 3 attempts
- task queue queries failed with `TASK_QUERY_FAILED`

Docker reported `Up ... (healthy)`, the control plane reported `running` with a current heartbeat and zero errors, and no automated recovery fired. Restarting the one container immediately restored database, conversation, and authenticated streamed-chat operations. This is a production-promotion blocker because a false-green agent cannot serve any DB-backed interaction.

Incident receipt: `projects/eliza-fleet/STAGING-INCIDENT-2026-07-18-EVENING.md` (operator-side evidence; 2026-07-18 22:21Z through 2026-07-19 00:12Z).

## Scope

Implement an end-to-end liveness contract for terminal database closure:

1. Agent readiness/liveness must exercise the database, not infer health from process/runtime state alone.
2. A terminal PGlite closed/shutdown result must make liveness unhealthy.
3. The provisioning/supervisor path must consume that unhealthy result and restart/recover the agent/container.
4. Bounded transient DB errors must not cause restart loops. Distinguish terminal closure from transient probe failures, apply backoff, and enforce a restart budget/cooldown.
5. Preserve auth, billing, local-state durability, and existing persistence/restore behavior.

## Reproduction and proof required

- Close a real PGlite adapter after successful boot.
- Prove readiness/liveness flips red while the process remains alive.
- Prove the supervisor recovery path fires for terminal closure.
- Prove transient probe failures do not immediately restart and repeated recovery is budgeted/backed off.
- Focused agent health and provisioning-worker tests, plus exact endpoint payload/state-transition evidence.

## Block-0 duplicate check

Searched open issues, open PRs, and Project 12 for `PGlite is closed`, DB health/liveness/readiness, and auto-restart. Related but non-duplicative:

- #16309 / #16311 cover fresh-boot service/schema/scheduler failures, not a post-boot terminally closed adapter or supervisor recovery.
- #15228 covers stale pid-1 lock crash loops where the process exits/restarts, not a live process with false-green DB health.
- #15603 and #15783 cover hosted-agent hardening and off-box durability, not this liveness failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] DB-exercising readiness/liveness reports terminally closed PGlite as unhealthy.
- [ ] Supervisor/provisioning consumes the signal and performs bounded recovery.
- [ ] Terminal vs transient classification is explicit and tested.
- [ ] Backoff plus restart budget prevents hot restart loops.
- [ ] Real-PGlite close reproduction and recovery-path tests pass.
- [ ] No auth, billing, or durability weakening.

- canonical work, team, agent, and session identity

topPRs.title: fix: recover terminally closed PGlite agents
topPRs.author: 0xSolace
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #16650.

A dedicated agent could keep process/container health green while its embedded PGlite was terminally closed, leaving all DB-backed operations dead until a manual restart. This PR makes database liveness an exercised end-to-end contract and gives the fleet supervisor a bounded recovery path.

- perform a real `SELECT 1` in runtime and cloud-agent health paths
- classify terminal PGlite closure separately from transient probe failures
- return HTTP 503 with `ready: false` and `canRespond: false` on terminal closure
- expose DB liveness in cloud-agent health and status RPC payloads
- consume terminal DB health in fleet heartbeat and enqueue the existing deduplicated restart job
- bound recovery to three restarts per one-hour window with a ten-minute cooldown
- keep transient failures on normal retry/hysteresis, with no immediate restart
- isolate the DB recovery budget from unrelated shared `error_count` uses
- make PGlite `isReady()` exercise the database rather than cached manager state

No auth, billing, backup/restore, persistence, or state-durability behavior is weakened.

## Incident proof

The regression test starts a real in-memory PGlite, proves `/api/health` is green, closes PGlite while the runtime remains alive, and proves health flips to HTTP 503 with terminal DB state. Supervisor tests prove terminal recovery enqueue, transient suppression, cooldown, and budget exhaustion.

Receipt: `PGLITE-LIVENESS-RECOVERY-2026-07-18.md`

## Tests

- `packages/agent`: focused real-PGlite health route, **1 passed**
- `packages/app-core`: cloud-agent DB liveness classification, **5 passed**
- `packages/cloud/shared`: recovery, transient, cooldown, budget tests, **5 passed**, 104 filtered

topPRs.title: fix(discord): durable turn/outbox state machine for exactly-once reply (stacked on #16696)
topPRs.author: 0xSolace
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Durable turn / outbox state machine that closes the crash window **deliberately
left open by #16696**. #16696 suppresses a duplicate inbound Discord turn once
the inbound memory is persisted. That fixed double-dispatch but left a worse
gap: a crash **after inbound persistence but before the outbound reply** caused
permanent replay suppression, so the message was ingested and **no reply was
ever sent** (SOLIZA cutover charter rows **D4/D5**).

> ⚠️ **Stacked on #16696** (`sol/discord-inbound-idempotency`). Review the top
> commit only; base #16696 first. If #16696 merges, rebasing this onto `develop`
> is a no-op on the shared lines.

## Design

Add a durable turn record keyed by the Discord message id with an explicit
lifecycle:

```
RECEIVED ──▶ DISPATCHED ──▶ REPLIED   (terminal)
                    └──────▶ FAILED    (terminal, retries exhausted)
```

On redelivery / process restart, instead of blindly returning when the inbound
memory exists:

- **terminal (REPLIED / FAILED)** → genuine no-op
- **non-terminal + a reply memory already exists** → reconcile to REPLIED, **no
  resend**
- **non-terminal, no reply, retry budget remains** → **resume** the reply path
- **retry budget exhausted** → explicit terminal **FAILED** (no silent drop)

### Delivery model: send-then-record + reconcile probe (documented choice)

The connector already writes a durable **outbound reply memory** for every
message it emits (`content.inReplyTo = <inbound id>`,
`metadata.platformMessageId = <discord reply id>`). That reply memory **is** the
authoritative record-of-send. Rather than add a second "reserved-before-send"
outbox row that can itself desync from Discord on a crash, we **reconcile
against the reply memory the send path already produces**: before re-dispatching
a resumed turn we probe for an existing reply to this inbound; if one exists the
reply already went out (crash in the send↔record gap) and we reconcile to
REPLIED without resending. Bounded retries are safe because the send path is
content-idempotent via #15601's outbound reservation and #13054's outbound
memory dedupe.

The **#16696 pre-persistence retry semantics are preserved**: a failure before
the durable claim leaves nothing persisted and stays retryable.

## Validation

Focused Vitest, run **green locally** in the worktree (`bun install` + generated
i18n keywords):

```
✓ plugins/plugin-discord/__tests__/turn-state.test.ts (11 tests)
✓ plugins/plugin-discord/__tests__/messages-inbound-idempotency.test.ts (5 tests)
✓ plugins/plugin-discord/__tests__/messages-durable-turn.test.ts (6 tests)
Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  22 passed (22)
```

Full discord messages regression lane (65 tests) also green.

Crash-simulation coverage (mandated cases): (a) crash after persist before
dispatch → resume replies once; (b) crash after dispatch before reply record →
resume replies once, no double send; (b2) reply already delivered before crash →
reconcile, no resend; (c) redelivery after REPLIED → no-op; (d) bounded retry
exhaustion → terminal FAILED, no silent drop; plus pre-persistence failure stays
retryable.

- `bunx @biomejs/biome check` on touched files: pass
- `git diff --check`: pass

Co-authored-by: wakesync <shadow@shad0w.xyz>

Signed-off-by: [sol-orch]

topPRs.title: feat(agent): bounded memory retention for the append-only memory partitions
topPRs.author: 0xSolace
topPRs.body:
## What

Bounded retention for the append-only core memory partitions (`memories` + the `embeddings` that cascade with them). These grow one row per turn/fact/fragment/document forever with no upstream pruning — the failure class behind an unbounded-PGlite disk-fill. Nothing in the runtime bounds them today.

## Growth surfaces (audit)

| table | growth | prior bound | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `memories` | 1 row / turn·fact·fragment·doc | none | **age + count prune** |
| `embeddings` | 1:1 w/ memories, up to ~12KB/row (3072-dim) | cascade-on-memory-delete only | pruned via cascade in `deleteManyMemories` |
| `logs` | 1 row / structured log | cascade on entity/room delete only | out of scope (flagged for follow-up — biggest table empirically) |
| `central_messages` | 1 row / message | cascade on channel delete only | out of scope (flagged) |
| `memory_access_logs` | append-only | none | out of scope (flagged) |

`memories`/`embeddings` is the dominant always-growing surface (every turn), so it is addressed first. Empirically on a scratch DB after a smoke run, `logs` was actually the largest table (736 rows / 2.4 MB vs memories 188 rows / 288 KB) — flagged as the next retention target.

## Design

- `memory-retention.ts` — **pure, deterministic planner.** Two orthogonal bounds per (room, partition): age (`retentionDays`) and count (`maxRowsPerRoom`). A row is evicted iff *either* bound would evict it; the newest rows are always preserved. Deletion set is oldest-first and clamp-able (`maxDeletePerSweep`). **OFF by default** — no active bound yields an empty plan, so merging this changes no behavior until an operator opts in.
- `memory-retention-service.ts` — registered runtime `Service`. Resolves config from `getSetting` (host-folded) with a `process.env` fallback; schedules a sweep only when a bound is active (unref'd timers, re-entrancy guard, restart-safe with no persisted cursor). Batches deletes through the adapter's `deleteManyMemories`, which drops each memory's embeddings in the same transaction. Scope is the canonical memory partitions only — never `logs`, `central_messages`, or auth-audit tables.

## Config (all optional; absent ⇒ bound disabled)

```
ELIZA_MEMORY_RETENTION_DAYS
ELIZA_MEMORY_RETENTION_MAX_ROWS_PER_ROOM
ELIZA_MEMORY_RETENTION_MAX_DELETE_PER_SWEEP
ELIZA_MEMORY_RETENTION_INTERVAL_MINUTES   # default 360 (6h)
```

## Tests — 20/20 green

`vitest run packages/agent/src/runtime/memory-retention.test.ts`

Planner: off-by-default, non-positive-bounds-disabled, age bound, count bound, both bounds, per-room isolation, oldest-first ordering + clamp, missing-timestamp keep-safe, config parsing. Service (fake adapter): off-by-default no-op, synthetic 500-row growth → prune keeps the bound with newest surviving, age prune, **ONLY memory partitions touched (no logs/central_messages/auth-audit)**, shared per-sweep delete budget across partitions, restart-safe/idempotent, re-entrancy guard, safe `stop()`.

## Evidence

<!-- evidence-row:after-screenshots -->
- [ ] After screenshots `N/A - backend-only change, no UI surface`.
